references.text: In the immediate context, Jesus makes similar demands on discipleship: to put him before family ([ref:Luk 14:26|Luke 14:26]) and to carry one's own cross ([ref:Luk 14:27|Luke 14:27]). Verse 33 summarizes and reinforces these demands by including everything one owns.

The two parables about counting the cost—the tower builder ([ref:Luk 14:28-30|Luke 14:28–30]) and the king who goes to war ([ref:Luk 14:31-32|Luke 14:31–32])—illustrate precisely the point of verse 33: one must carefully consider what discipleship costs, namely everything one has.

Jesus tells the rich man to sell all he owns and give it to the poor in order to follow him. When the man became sorrowful, Jesus commented on how difficult it is for the wealthy to enter the kingdom of God ([ref:Luk 18:22-23|Luke 18:22–23]). This clarifies the demand in 14:33 to renounce all one possesses.

Jesus urges his disciples to sell what they own and give gifts to the poor, and to store up treasures in heaven ([ref:Luk 12:33|Luke 12:33]). The same idea of detaching oneself from earthly possessions to follow Jesus.

After Peter, James, and John had pulled their boats onto land, they left everything and followed Jesus ([ref:Luk 5:11|Luke 5:11]). A concrete example of renouncing all one owns to become a disciple of Jesus.
Levi left everything and followed Jesus ([ref:Luk 5:28|Luke 5:28]). Another example of someone who actually fulfilled the requirement to give up their possessions.

Peter says that the disciples have left everything to follow Jesus. Jesus promises that anyone who has left houses, brothers, sisters, or fields for his name's sake will receive a hundred times as much ([ref:Matt 19:27-29|Matthew 19:27–29]). This confirms that renouncing all is a fundamental requirement of discipleship.

Paul counted everything he once considered gain as loss for the sake of Christ, and regarded all things as worthless in order to win Christ ([ref:Fil 3:7-8|Philippians 3:7–8]). An apostolic testimony to renouncing all to belong to Christ.

Jesus says that whoever loves father or mother more than him is not worthy of him, and whoever does not take up their cross and follow him is not worthy of him ([ref:Matt 10:37-38|Matthew 10:37–38]). A parallel demand for discipleship as in Luke 14:33.

The first Christians had everything in common and sold their possessions to share with those in need ([ref:Apg 2:44-45|Acts 2:44–45]). A practical expression of the radical discipleship Jesus requires in Luke 14:33.
